added.text: All eight analog channels meet the declared range, accuracy and acquisition requirements while wheel-speed capture, IMU/GNSS, CAN, BLE and logging operate concurrently. Verify the selected wheel sensors over their declared speed range and exercise the specified sensor-fault cases.

Standalone logging meets its declared duration and data-integrity requirements without a phone, including power interruption and full-media tests. Verify the selected digital tire-sensor interface over the declared harness and record the actual sensor/zone coverage.

A joint GPIO, SPI/bus and 35-pin connector allocation covering the MCP3208, both wheel-speed inputs, digital tire sensors, storage, existing IMU/GNSS/CAN and debug access. Preserve existing ECU connector assignments and CAN frame definitions; allocate new telemetry messages separately.

Wheel sensor type, voltage/current interface, maximum pulse frequency, low-speed behavior and conditioning. The owner has no wheel sensors or tone rings selected; develop a sensor-and-conditioning recommendation. Support for Hall and VR together is not yet a requirement.
Digital tire sensor protocol, mounting and field of view, zone count, harness length and update rate. No specific tire sensor has been selected.
Logging duration, data format, timestamp source, retrieval method, media endurance and power-loss behavior. Storage must coexist with BLE OTA and the sealed enclosure.
Expanded power and thermal budgets, including sensor faults and storage/radio peaks; define supply-voltage monitoring, sensor-supply fault detection and feasible open/short diagnostics.

Full connector courtyard and module antenna keep-outs, mounting-hole clearances and enclosure fit. Start with the current 90 × 65 mm pilot outline; unchanged dimensions are a layout target, not a demonstrated fit. TE drawing 776163 K1 gives 76.9 mm overall header width; 63.4 mm is not its overall width.
The owner accepted the capability baseline on 2026-10-20. The following implementation choices remain open; the generator must not silently invent them:

Manufacturer references: [MCP3204/3208 datasheet](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/APID/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/21298e.pdf) and [TE 776163-1 product and drawing](https://www.te.com/en/product-776163-1.html).

The previous v9 schematic, PCB, BOM, io-map and compiled interface contract remain historical pilot artifacts. Their passing checks do not establish compliance with Revision 3. Regenerate the expanded candidate from revised source inputs and repeat placement, routing and review.

| Digital tire temperature | Provide an external digital interface for front and rear tire-temperature sensors. Resolve protocol, channel/zone count, sensor power, cable length and protection before assigning pins. Provision does not establish compatibility with arbitrary sensors. |

| Standalone logging | Record pod measurements and received ECU telemetry without a phone connection. Target eight hours of recording as a soft capacity goal, with wireless download while parked (owner clarification 2026-10-20). Report achieved duration against the declared workload; shorter duration is a disclosed tradeoff, not an automatic failure. Define throughput, timestamps, full-media behavior and recovery from interrupted power before selecting storage. |

| Wheel speed | Two independently conditioned pulse inputs for front and rear wheel speed. Resolve Hall, VR or dual-mode support and the sensor electrical requirements before choosing the conditioning circuit. |

Retain reverse-polarity and automotive-transient protection. Coordinate the clamp, input disconnect/protection, capacitor ratings and regulator absolute maxima using the actual pulse voltage, duration and source impedance. A nominal TVS voltage alone does not establish survival.

Define a continuous-operation voltage range, a short-dip ride-through envelope and a lower-voltage controlled-reset region separately. Check both electronics and powered sensors: a running MCU does not establish valid sensor data during a supply dip.

Specify and validate input filtering and damping over the regulator's load range, including radio and storage bursts. Measure ripple at the connector, logic rails, sensor supply and ADC reference; set limits from regulator stability and acquisition error budgets.

Add independent input/rail monitoring and a power-fail/reset supervisor path. Use hysteresis to avoid repeated resets during marginal supply. Record supply faults and invalidate affected sensor samples.

Define bounded log loss on abrupt power removal, storage recovery and restart behavior. Calculate hold-up energy from measured worst-case consumption and storage completion time before claiming a safe flush; capacitors do not cover indefinite brownouts.

Recalculate sensor-rail current and thermal limits. The pilot's TPS7B4253-Q1 rail is rated for 300 mA and had a 200 mA aggregate sensor budget; it is not prequalified for the expansion. Evaluate separately protected sensor branches so an external sensor fault does not unnecessarily collapse the logger.

Owner direction, 2026-10-20: redesign the power block to accommodate brownouts and ripple as well as the expanded sensor load. The owner reports possible unusual SV650 supply behavior around 2,500 rpm. This is an investigation lead, not a measured waveform or established model-wide defect.

Verification must include programmable supply dips/recovery, swept ripple, sensor shorts and load steps while acquiring and logging. Capture the actual bike supply at the pod harness around 2,500 rpm, across the operating range and during starting, then replay relevant measured disturbances on the bench. Keep simulation, injected-waveform testing and on-bike evidence distinct. No specific ripple amplitude or dip duration has yet been established.
Reference design for topology and test methods: [TI TIDA-00699 automotive front end](https://www.ti.com/tool/TIDA-00699). Its reported results apply to that reference design, not this pod.
On 2026-10-20, the owner approved retaining the following parts despite the blanket 105 °C component-rating requirement, with enclosure thermal validation required:

The assembly verifier's canonical source is
[operating-temperature-exemptions.txt](operating-temperature-exemptions.txt).
That file contains only the three owner-approved exemption lines, without
Markdown, headings, comments or blank lines. Cite its captured bytes, SHA-256 and
individual line numbers in the expanded pod scope. Withdraw an exemption by
deleting its line and regenerating the scope citations.

These declarations waive the blanket 105 °C part-selection check only. They do not qualify operation beyond manufacturer limits, waive thermal validation, or transfer to a different part/reference. Record the exception with each exact component binding. Validate enclosure temperatures and self-heating under worst-case input, sensor load, radio and logging activity; the stated +85 °C board-ambient ceiling is not demonstrated for this assembly. If the actual thermal margin is insufficient, revise cooling, the operating envelope or the affected part with an explicit disposition before release.

The current exemption mechanism excludes these references from the assembly
operating-temperature predicate entirely; it does not verify them against their
own ratings. Therefore the expanded scope must carry actual manufacturer limits,
exact-part binding and enclosure thermal validation as unresolved declared
limitations. A passing assembly predicate does not discharge those obligations.
The scope fragment in
[expansion/temperature-scope-fragment.json](expansion/temperature-scope-fragment.json)
retains the citations and limitations for incorporation when the expanded scope
is generated; it is not a completed assembly check.
| U1 | ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N8 | Retain the 85 °C module variant. |
| U2 | LSM6DSO32TR | Retain the 85 °C IMU. |
| U4 | MCP3208-BI/SL | Retain the industrial-temperature ADC for the expanded design; this does not approve the old MCP3204 binding. |

changed.after: The pod also relays every CAN1 frame it receives from the ECU to RaceChrono over the BLE DIY CAN characteristic, filtered to the IDs RaceChrono subscribes to. The eight analog channels are 12-bit and use a reference derived from the pod's own 5 V sensor supply (see Interfaces). Ratiometric sensors track that supply; absolute-voltage sensors require their own transfer-function and reference-error treatment. The pod is a standalone unit with its own power supply; the ECU's 5V\_SENSOR\_2 rail is not used.

changed.after: Board outline sized to fit inside the rear seat cowl (the earlier 80 mm by 50 mm figure was not an owner requirement; owner decision 2026-10-19: "I don't know how the size got fixed. I didn't specify, there's room in the cowl, that said, a double-sided part seems fine"), double-sided component placement permitted (preserving the ESP32 module antenna keep-out, the F.Cu over In1.Cu GNSS RF path, and connector mechanical constraints), mounting holes in all four corners. The earlier 12 mm component-height limit was an agent-drafted assumption, not an owner requirement (owner correction 2026-10-20: "I never set 12mm, that was arbitrary."). Actual enclosure/cowl height clearance remains unknown and must be measured; 12 mm is not a hard pass/fail limit, and no connector-specific exception is pending. The rear seat cowl is large, so the envelope is not tight.
changed.before: Board envelope 80 mm by 50 mm or smaller, component height 12 mm or less above the board, mounting holes in all four corners. The rear seat cowl is large, so the envelope is not tight.

changed.after: Enclosure sealed to IP67, non-metallic over the ESP32 module antenna, with the harness connector and the SMA antenna connector the only penetrations. Do not pot the pod unless proven necessary (potting detunes the ESP32 module antenna and GNSS RF path and mechanically stresses the MEMS IMU package); rigidly couple the board and IMU to the enclosure and the enclosure to the frame so the IMU measures the bike, not a floating board.
